false_positive_dispositions.reason: Required const virtual callback is invoked on a privately owned, originally non-const Core.
false_positive_dispositions.comment: False positive at src/editor/editor_core.cpp:814: this std::bad_alloc handler is inside the pinned NotifyParent(NotificationData&) const noexcept override (Scintilla Editor.h:492). EditorControl privately owns Core as std::unique_ptr<Core> (editor_control.h:137-144), and constructs it with std::make_unique<Core>(*this, selectionOptions) (editor_control.cpp:71). It does not modify an originally const object. Changing the callback's const qualification would break the required override.

false_positive_dispositions.comment: False positive at src/editor/platform/parallel_tasks.h:22: this partial-startup handler transports the primary batch exception with std::current_exception; it does not treat the failure as a successful result. RunAsync drains every started task through future.get(), then calls std::rethrow_exception(failure) at line 32. Startup failure deliberately remains primary if an already-started worker also fails. An immediate rethrow would skip explicit result collection from the remaining tasks. Deferred propagation completes every started task before the error crosses the batch boundary. false_positive_dispositions.message: Use "std::print" instead of "fprintf".
false_positive_dispositions.reason: The recommended std::print is unavailable in the supported GCC 13 standard library.
false_positive_dispositions.comment: False positive for the supported compiler baseline at tests/surface_initialization.cpp:417. This fprintf diagnostic is built on Linux with GCC 13: .github/actions/dependencies/action.yml installs gcc-13/g++-13 and exports CXX=g++-13. The recommendation specifically requires std::print. GCC's libstdc++ implementation table lists P2093R14 formatted output as first available in GCC 14.1, and the GCC 14 release notes list std::print/std::println as additions. Replacing this fixed-format diagnostic with std::print would break the supported GCC 13 build. Sources: https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/libstdc++/manual/status.html and https://gcc.gnu.org/gcc-14/changes.html .

false_positive_dispositions.message: Replace the use of "new" with an operation that automatically manages the memory.
false_positive_dispositions.reason: wxWidgets top-level frame ownership with deferred Destroy, not a manually leaked object.
false_positive_dispositions.comment: False positive at tests/surface_initialization.cpp:562: the EditorFrame is a wxWidgets top-level window whose lifetime is managed by the native application. The presentation callback calls frame->Destroy() at line 571 after successful checks or a caught test failure, then exits the loop. In the pinned wxWidgets 3.3.3 implementation, wxTopLevelWindowBase::Destroy queues the window for deferred deletion; wxAppConsoleBase::DeletePendingObjects deletes queued objects, and wxAppBase::DeleteAllTLWs cleans remaining top-level windows at shutdown. A local unique_ptr would destroy the frame when OnInit returns while the asynchronous presentation callback still uses it. Sources: wxWidgets v3.3.3 src/common/toplvcmn.cpp:102-117, appbase.cpp:643, appcmn.cpp:129.
